key_insight: A black-box attack called immrag can mine multimodal RAG systems by steering image-based queries toward previously unrecovered datastore items, exposing a new extraction risk beyond text prompts.
clinical_relevance: For medical imaging RAG tools, this means private radiology images could potentially be reconstructed from the retrieval system, creating a confidentiality and governance concern for clinical deployments.
method: Attack embeds malicious instructions inside an attacker-held image rather than text.
Each query mixes a shadow image with a previously recovered image to discover new retrievals.
Relevance-weighted resampling adaptively shifts subsequent queries toward unexplored regions of embedding space.
evidence_signal: In black-box tests across multiple CLIP-family retrievers, a 2500-query run recovered up to 611 distinct radiology images and outperformed a non-adaptive baseline by up to 5.6x.
watch_item: The results show extraction risk under experimental settings, but real-world impact may vary with system design, retrieval defenses, and how image-returning MRAG is implemented.
paper_title: Walking the Embedding Space: Datastore Extraction from Multimodal RAG
